meta.title: Use of Glassware Washer in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To clean and decontaminate laboratory glassware used in crude drug extraction, phytochemical analysis, and standardization to prevent cross-contamination between experiments.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for cleaning all non-volumetric glassware after use in extraction, phytochemical screening, and histological staining procedures.
procedure: Collect all used glassware in a designated sink area — separate glassware by contamination type: organic solvent residue, coloured stain, acid/base, and general aqueous.
Pre-rinse all glassware with the same solvent used in the experiment before washing with water — this dissolves residues that are insoluble in water (resinous extracts, oil-based stains).
For glassware with coloured plant stains (turmeric, phenolics): soak in 70% ethanol for 15–30 minutes before washing.
For glassware with resin or wax residue: soak in petroleum ether or hexane, discard solvent as chemical waste, then wash with detergent.
Prepare warm (40–50°C) detergent solution using laboratory-grade glassware cleaning detergent (e.g., Extran, Decon).
Scrub inner surfaces vigorously with appropriate size bottle brushes; swab test tubes with cotton-tipped swabs for narrow necks.
Scrub exterior surfaces with a sponge or cloth.
Rinse three times with warm tap water — ensure all detergent traces are removed (residual detergent affects phytochemical colour reactions).
Perform final rinse with distilled water — at least two rinses.
Inspect each piece for cleanliness: water should drain uniformly without forming droplets; droplet formation indicates residual organic contamination.
Place cleaned glassware inverted on the glassware dryer rack.
Discard wash water containing organic solvents as chemical waste.
Clean the washing sink and surrounding area after each washing session.
precautions: Wear thick rubber gloves, safety goggles, and apron during glassware washing — risk of cuts from broken glass and chemical splashes.
Never use steel wool or abrasive scrubbers on volumetric markings — abrasion removes calibration graduations.
Inspect all glassware for cracks and chips before washing — cracked glassware should be discarded in a puncture-proof sharps bin, not the regular trash.
Do not mix incompatible wash solvents (acids and organic solvents) in the same wash basin.
Use chromic acid mixture (dichromate/sulfuric acid) only when absolutely necessary — it is highly toxic and carcinogenic; dispose of as hazardous waste.
Dispose of all solvent-contaminated wash water as chemical waste per institutional protocols.
Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after glassware washing — even after wearing gloves.
